statement: BARRIER GATE (target (8), width route). CHOPRS Thm 2 (arXiv:1911.08297, sec 1.3, fetched text): (B1-O) MCSP[2^{n^{1/3}},2^{n^{2/3}}] in Formula-O-XOR[N^{1.01}] with oracles of fan-in <= N^eps in the layer above the XOR leaves; (B3-O) InnerProduct on N bits is not computed by N^{2-3delta}-size Formula-O-XOR circuits with <= N^{2-3delta} oracle gates of fan-in N^delta, for ANY oracle. The locality barrier says lower-bound arguments of the B3/B4 type extend to such oracle circuits. Applied to the width route: the proved identity (Thm 8 eq.22, Lemma 10 eq.26) holds only for an oracle-free fixed linear kernel, and oracle gates remove the linear-overlap structure, so the identity does not transfer. STATUS: OPEN, neither YES nor NO. Not shown: the width argument is a localized argument (it has not been checked against the B3-O hypotheses for this exact method). Perfect-matching control: NOT CHECKED. Natural-measure test: NOT CHECKED. Decisive test: does a lower bound on the width of the restricted kernel survive when each linear gate is replaced by an arbitrary fan-in <= N^eps oracle gate? If it survives, the route is localized and blocked by the locality barrier; if it fails, the route is only as strong as the linear structure.

statement: Degree transfer from 3-colouring: for a graph G let T(G) be the positive 1-in-3 formula with clauses (x_v1,x_v2,x_v3) for every vertex v and (x_uc,x_wc,y_uwc) with a fresh variable for every edge uw and colour c. (a) T(G) is GF(3)-consistent for every G. (b) T(G) is satisfiable iff G is 3-colourable. (c) Over GF(2) modulo x^2 = x, if the XOR/carry system of T(G) (L = 1+a+b+c, q = ab+ac+bc per clause) has a polynomial-calculus refutation of degree d, then the standard 3-colouring encoding of G (sum_c x_vc = 1, x_vc x_vc' = 0, x_uc x_wc = 0) has one of degree max(d,2): substitute y_uwc := 1 + x_uc + x_wc (affine, degree-preserving); edge L maps to 0, edge q to x_uc x_wc, y^2+y to 0, vertex L to the vertex axiom, vertex q to a sum of the axioms x_vc x_vc'. CONSEQUENCE if (c) holds: the linear PC-degree lower bounds for 3-colouring of bounded-degree graphs over every field (Lauria-Nordstrom 2017) give an explicit infinite family of GF(3)-blind positive 1-in-3 formulas with PC degree Omega(n) and, by Impagliazzo-Pudlak-Sgall, PC size exp(Omega(n)) in the XOR/carry encoding over GF(2) - a class result for PC/Groebner-based procedures, not P != NP. statement: For every minimal unsatisfiable positive 1-in-3 family F (any n): blind(F) = 1 iff rank_GF(3)(A_F) = |F|, where A_F is the |F| x n incidence matrix over GF(3). statement: LEVEL 1a monotonicity lemma. Let h(y) = SAT(F(y)), where each triple T is an input x_T that is a constant 0/1 or a single hard-input bit y_j (no negation), and F(y) = {T : x_T = 1}. Then h is monotone decreasing in y, because F(y) is monotone in y and SAT is a down-set in the triple family: if F(y') is satisfiable and F(y) is a subfamily of F(y'), then F(y) is satisfiable. Consequences: (i) MOD_q for every q >= 2 is neither monotone nor antitone, so it is not a negation-free projection of SAT or of NOT-SAT; (ii) MAJ is monotone increasing, so NOT-SAT (monotone increasing) does not exclude it by this test; (iii) the test applies to negation-free projections only, not to AC0 reductions, which may compute non-monotone gadgets before feeding SAT.

structure.scope: Negation-free projections (constants and single triple bits, no negation) of the triple-indicator input. Says nothing about AC0 reductions with auxiliary gadgets, nor about Level 1b or Level 2. Derived by hand, not yet checked by the validator.

statement: Reduction lemma: an unused variable u in a positive 1-in-3 clause set F on n variables is free in every 0/1 and GF(3) condition. So F is GF(3)-blind with nullity k on n variables iff F restricted to the other n-1 variables is GF(3)-blind with nullity k-1 and covers them. Consequence: the kernel type of every unused-variable blind nullity-2 formula is forced to be (n-1)-1 whenever the reduced nullity-1 kernel vector has full support on the n-1 used variables. This full-support property holds for all 1,350 covering blind nullity-1 formulas at n=6 (m=4..7), which gives the 6-1 type at n=7. Whether full support is forced for all n is open.

statement: Transfer limit of the OGP -> circuit route (Q-5c20e15028). The Linial-Mansour-Nisan step needs the target Boolean function f to have Fourier weight concentrated on low degree. For AC0 circuits of size s and depth d, the weight above degree (log s)^{O(d)} is at most 1/poly, so the route can reach constant-depth classes. For general poly-size circuits there is no such concentration (parity has all its weight at degree n), so the route cannot reach P/poly through Fourier concentration alone. The limit is therefore the Fourier-concentration property of the circuit class, not the OGP property of the instance.

statement: Barrier analysis for Lemma (Kernel counting for linear F_2 realizations): This is a LOWER BOUND on space S for linear F_2 staged realizations solving search-MCSP. (1) Relativizing? The proof uses counting of circuits in the unrelativized world; it does not relativize (an oracle could add circuits to Y_s, changing the count). (2) Natural? The measure is space S of a linear F_2 streaming algorithm. A natural property in RR sense would be a property of the function's truth table decidable in poly(N) time that is large and constructive. Space complexity of a specific restricted model is a syntactic property of the algorithm, not a semantic property of the function. It is NOT natural in the RR sense. (3) Algebrizing? The proof is combinatorial (counting), not algebraic. (4) Localizing? The proof uses global counting over the whole kernel, not local properties. (5) Perfect-matching control: Perfect matching is in P. Does it have a linear F_2 streaming algorithm with sublinear space? Unknown, but even if it does, this bound is for search-MCSP specifically, not for all functions in P. The bound does NOT transfer to general circuits because the model is explicitly restricted to linear F_2 updates. This is a RESTRICTED MODEL lower bound, not a general circuit lower bound.

statement: Exact lemma (short proof): for a positive 1-in-3 clause set S, sat(S)=1 iff the GF(3) affine solution set of A x = 1 contains a 0/1 vector. Proof: a 0/1 solution of the integer system satisfies the GF(3) system. Conversely, a 0/1 vector with every clause sum congruent to 1 mod 3 has clause sum 1, because a sum of three bits lies in {0,1,2,3}. So the non-linear question is membership of {0,1}^n in an exact affine GF(3) space. For n=6 with rank3=5 the solution set has exactly 3 points, so the 0/1 test is a 3-candidate check. Mechanism for the counterexamples: cons3=1 and sat=0 occur exactly when none of the 3 points is 0/1.

structure.scope: Lemma holds for all n (proved above, for 3-element clauses). Mechanism is a finite hypothesis for n=6 rank3=5 only.
